name: Double Calendar Spread
summary: Two same-strike calendars at different strikes - a put calendar below spot and a call calendar above - widening the profit tent so the underlying can wander and still pay.

legs.strike_rule: Lower strike by delta: front put |delta| 0.25-0.35 (roughly 1 standard deviation lower boundary).
Upper strike by delta: front call delta 0.25-0.35; the two strikes should straddle spot roughly symmetrically (|put delta| within 0.07 of call delta).

max_profit: No closed form; two local peaks at the two strikes at front expiry. Typically 20-35% of the total debit, with a flatter, wider payoff than a single calendar.
max_loss: The total net debit paid, if the underlying finishes far outside both strikes (or, less commonly, if it sits exactly between them while vol collapses).
breakevens: Roughly lower strike - 1.0 x (debit per side) and upper strike + 1.0 x (debit per side), in underlying points; solve numerically with back-month IV at front expiry.

greeks.delta: ~0 when the strikes are delta-symmetric around spot
greeks.gamma: negative, but flatter and less peaked than a single calendar
greeks.theta: positive, roughly double the single calendar per unit of capital
greeks.vega: positive, roughly double a single calendar; the structure is meaningfully long back-month vol

when_to_use: IV rank < 30, flat-to-backwardated term structure, and a range-bound underlying whose expected move is wider than a single calendar's tent. Choose the double calendar over the single when the front-month expected move exceeds the single calendar's breakeven band - which is most of the time on liquid ETFs.
entry_rules: front_IV - back_IV >= -3.0 vol points at BOTH strikes.
Strikes by delta: front put |delta| 0.25-0.35, front call delta 0.25-0.35, and the two deltas within 0.07 of each other so the structure starts delta-neutral.
Strike spacing should bracket at least 1.0 x the front-month expected move (ATM straddle price).
Front 21-35 DTE, back 45-70 DTE, gap 21-35 days.
Total debit <= 3% of equity per unit; combined bid-ask <= 10% of the total debit.
No earnings or ex-dividend inside the front cycle.

LEVEL 3 OK: each short front leg is covered by the same-strike later-expiring long. Submit as one 4-leg mleg. Alpaca supports up to 4 legs; if the mixed-expiry 4-leg order is rejected, submit it as two 2-leg calendar mlegs, LONG legs filled first.
management_rules: Profit target +20% of total debit (the tent is wider but flatter than a single calendar, so take less).
Delta band: if |net delta| > 0.35 per unit, roll the untested short strike toward spot (never the tested one away).
When spot breaches either short strike by more than 0.5 x ATR(14), close that side's calendar and let the other side run as a single directional calendar, or close both.
Roll short legs out one expiry when front DTE <= 7 and both shorts' |delta| <= 0.60, for a net credit only.
exit_rules: Close or roll BOTH short legs by 14:30 ET on the front expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the whole structure no later than 2 trading days before front expiry if not rolling.
Close any short leg immediately when its extrinsic <= $0.05/share or its |delta| >= 0.90.
Close the short call before the session preceding ex-dividend if its extrinsic < the dividend per share.
Unwind short legs before long legs, always.
If either long back-month leg marks below $0.10, close that calendar entirely.
assignment_risk: Both short front legs. The tested side is the one to watch: a trending underlying pushes one short deep ITM while the other decays to zero. The same-strike back-month long covers each short, so the worst case is a covered stock position, but the system must flatten any assignment within one session.
buying_power: Net debit only; no additional maintenance. Alpaca reserves the total debit.
liquidity_needs: Four legs means four spreads to cross. OI >= 250 per leg, underlying ADV >= 3M shares, and the total package must fill within 10% of the mid. ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM, XLF, EEM) are the natural home; avoid single stocks with wide chains.
common_mistakes: Setting the strikes too close together (you have just paid double for a single calendar's payoff); ignoring that the structure is double long vega in a falling-vol tape; rolling the tested side away from spot and turning a defined-risk trade into a chase; four-leg slippage quietly eating the entire profit target.
zero_dte_notes: A 0DTE double day calendar (0DTE shorts, 1-4 DTE longs, both sides) is viable on SPY/QQQ under the day-calendar rules at half size per side, with the same 14:30 ET forced close.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
also_filed_under: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
